## The device deciding how much to draw

64 candidates, 96 vertices each, 8 blocks of unrelated work on a second queue.
Cycles, so that a synchronisation costs what it stops.

| Visible | Drawn | No cull | Culled | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100% | 64 of 64 | 11,064 | 11,304 | **+2.2%** |
| 100% | 64 of 64 | 11,064 | 11,304 | **+2.2%** |
| 89% | 57 of 64 | 11,064 | 10,212 | **-7.7%** |
| 45% | 29 of 64 | 11,064 | 5,844 | **-47.2%** |

### What deciding on the device removes

Reading the count back means draining every queue, so the synchronisation
costs whatever the other one still had to do.

| Other work | Host reads the count | Device decides | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 blocks | 9,267 | 9,267 | **+0.0%** |
| 4 blocks | 9,672 | 9,672 | **+0.0%** |
| 16 blocks | 11,292 | 11,292 | **+0.0%** |
| 64 blocks | 17,772 | 17,772 | **+0.0%** |
| 256 blocks | 43,692 | 43,692 | **+0.0%** |

Nothing at all when the other queue had nothing, which is the honest shape of
it: an indirect launch buys the overlap a synchronisation would have thrown away.
